name: Talkspace
summary: Online therapy platform providing licensed psychotherapy via messaging and live video sessions. Best for depression, anxiety, and stress in medically stable adults.
description: Talkspace is a large online therapy platform that connects adults with licensed therapists through secure messaging and live video sessions. Users choose a subscription plan with weekly messaging and optional live sessions. Talkspace provides psychotherapy only (no primary prescribing) and is appropriate for mild to moderate depression, anxiety, and stress. It is not a crisis service, is not recommended for severe psychiatric conditions, and should not replace higher-level care when safety is a concern.
patient_summary: Talkspace offers online therapy with licensed therapists using secure messages and optional weekly live video. It’s convenient if you have mild to moderate depression or anxiety and want therapy from home. It does not prescribe medication (except through separate psychiatry services in some states), and it is not appropriate if you’re in crisis, have severe symptoms, or need emergency care.

efficacy_data.patient_text: Studies of online psychotherapy (not specific to Talkspace) show similar benefits to in-person therapy for many adults with depression and anxiety. Talkspace follows this model but does not yet have large independent randomized trials of its specific platform.

data_shared: Past reports and criticism regarding data sharing for marketing have been documented publicly
privacy_rating.certification: Subject to heightened scrutiny and public discussion regarding mental health data privacy

sections.heading: What Talkspace Does
sections.text: Talkspace connects adults with licensed therapists for psychotherapy via secure messaging and live sessions. Users subscribe monthly and can message their therapist throughout the week, with live video depending on plan. It’s convenient and accessible, but is not suitable for emergencies or severe psychiatric symptoms requiring in-person evaluation.

sections.heading: How Well Does Online Therapy Work?
sections.comparison: Internet-based CBT vs in-person CBT (not Talkspace-specific)
sections.text: Meta-analyses show online and video-based psychotherapy can produce symptom reduction similar to in-person CBT for depression and anxiety in many adults.
sections.patient_text: Online therapy can help many people with depression or anxiety, but Talkspace itself does not yet have large independent randomized trials.
